cases.note: one put at the delta exactly
one put just beyond: slow transit or a clock behind cannot be told apart
a stamp ahead at the delta exactly
a stamp ahead beyond the delta: no transit causes it
a later stamp ahead beyond the delta withdraws the trust a close one gave (F-102)
late puts behind by more than the delta do not withdraw it: transit cannot be told from drift

description: freshness.v1 §2.6, ground 2 (0.2): the offsets a reader measured of one stamping clock during one reading (each: its own clock at receipt of a live put, minus the put's stamp, in seconds; negative when the stamp is ahead), and the delta -> whether the reader trusts its clock against that clock. Trusted when the offset closest to zero is within the delta (inclusive), and no offset is below minus the delta: transit only adds to an offset, so a stamp ahead by more than the delta proves the clocks disagree. No offset at all is not trusted. Seconds are compared exactly, to the nanosecond.
